title: Optimize consumer concurrency and graceful retry semantics for Redis/Kafka workers
creator: Priya Sharma
description:
Problem:
Our consumer fleet occasionally experiences long tail latencies and transient throughput collapse under bursty load. Two main causes observed: (1) the Redis-backed lease and task visibility layer uses a synchronous client path that can block worker threads during network stalls, amplifying head-of-line blocking; (2) our retry semantics are decentralized and lack a shared budget, which allows noisy retries to create retry storms and move messages directly to the DLQ without graceful backoff coordination.

Goal:
Refactor the worker adapters and centralize backpressure and retry controls so that: (a) worker concurrency is enforced via non-blocking concurrency gates and connection pooling; (b) retries are governed by a RetryBudget with fast/slow buckets and circuit-breaker style fallback; (c) Redis client and Kafka consumer libraries are upgraded to the latest async-friendly releases and swapped to pooled async connectors where possible; (d) metrics and alerting are extended to catch regressions (queue_depth, retry_rate, p99_processing_latency, dlq_rate).

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: refactor core consumer loop for Redis and Kafka adapters, introduce shared retry-broker, upgrade redis/kafka client dependencies, add integration tests and benchmark harness, rollout plan with canaries.
- Out of scope: changing message schemas, adding new persistence layers, or altering upstream producers.
tasks: Spike: benchmark current consumer with synthetic bursts (done)
Design: retry budget and backoff policy (retry_budget.md)
Implement: non-blocking concurrency gate and per-partition semaphores
Upgrade: redis client to async pooled client and add connection pool metrics
Upgrade: kafka client to latest stable async consumer and test rebalance behavior
Implement: centralized RetryBudget and DLQ throttler
Tests: unit, integration, and chaos tests simulating Redis/Kafka stalls
Performance: run end-to-end QPS/latency benchmarks and record baselines
Rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback criteria
acceptance_criteria: Average consumer throughput for burst test improves >= 15% with same CPU allocation
P99 processing latency reduces by at least 20% under realistic burst profiles
Retry storms are eliminated: retry_rate per-minute falls by >= 50% during bursts
No increase in DLQ write-rate after rollouts (DLQ_rate stable or lower)
All new behavior covered by unit and integration tests; chaos tests show graceful degradation
Production canary rollout completes without triggering rollback alarms

2025-01-22 Maya P (Review): Code review notes: make semaphore ownership explicit and add metrics for 'semaphore_wait_seconds'. Also flagged potential cascade if retry budget refill rates are too aggressive.
